title: F5 BIG-IP APM: attackers can run their own code
verdictReason: Attacks are confirmed. The vulnerability is 47 days old, so many systems are likely still unpatched. It affects a product that faces the internet or gives remote access. The severity score is critical (9.3).
rankWhy: Exploitation is confirmed by an authoritative source.
The product faces the internet or gives remote access.

category.label: VPN, firewall or gateway
category.why: It sits at the edge of your network and faces the internet, so attackers can reach it directly.
category.doThis: If you have it, patch it today. If you cannot, block access to it from the internet until you can.

summary: F5 BIG-IP APM contains a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability when access policy and an OAuth profile are configured on a virtual server. This vulnerability could allow an unauthenticated attacker to perform remote code execution.
fix: CISA's instruction: apply the vendor's fix, or stop using the product if no fix exists. The deadline CISA set for US federal agencies, Sep 25, 2026, has passed. It is a US government deadline; use it as a guide.
